data.title: Amigurumi sphere — basic increase/decrease
data.source: seed sample, written for this repo
data.text:
Materials: worsted weight cotton, 3.5 mm hook, polyfill stuffing.

Abbreviations: ch = chain, sc = single crochet, inc = 2 sc in one st, dec = sc2tog, st(s) = stitch(es).

Work in continuous rounds. Do not join.

Rnd 1: 6 sc in a magic ring (6)
Rnd 2: inc in each st around (12)
Rnd 3: [sc, inc] x6 (18)
Rnd 4: [2 sc, inc] x6 (24)
Rnds 5-8: sc in each st around (24)
Rnd 9: [2 sc, dec] x6 (18)
Rnd 10: [sc, dec] x6 (12)
Stuff firmly, then Rnd 11: dec x6 (6)
Fasten off, leaving a long tail. Weave the tail through the front loops of the remaining 6 sts and pull closed.

data.title: Granny square — rounds with corner groups
data.source: seed sample, written for this repo
data.text:
Hook: 4.0 mm. Yarn: DK weight acrylic in three colours (A, B, C).

Gauge: one completed round measures 7 cm across.

With Colour A, ch 4 and join with a sl st to form a ring.

Rnd 1: ch 3 (counts as first dc), 2 dc in ring, ch 2, *3 dc in ring, ch 2* three times, join with sl st to top of ch 3. (12 dc, 4 ch-2 spaces)
Rnd 2: join Colour B in any ch-2 space. Ch 3, 2 dc in same space, ch 2, 3 dc in same space, *ch 1, [3 dc, ch 2, 3 dc] in next ch-2 space* around, ch 1, join. (24 dc)
Rnd 3: join Colour C in any corner space. Repeat Rnd 2, working 3 dc into each ch-1 space along the sides. (36 dc)

Finishing: fasten off, weave in all ends, block lightly to square up the corners.

data.title: Ribbed beanie — worked flat then seamed
data.source: seed sample, written for this repo
data.text:
Yarn: Aran weight wool, approx 180 m. Hook: 5.0 mm. Gauge: 14 sts x 12 rows = 10 cm in hdc blo.

Brim
Ch 31.
Row 1: hdc in 2nd ch from hook and in each ch across, turn. (30 sts)
Row 2: ch 1 (does not count as a st), hdc blo in each st across, turn. (30 sts)
Rows 3-60: repeat Row 2.

Body
Row 61: ch 1, hdc in each st across, turn. (30 sts)
Rows 62-70: repeat Row 61.

Assembly
Fold the panel in half and sl st the two short edges together. Run a gathering thread through the top edge, cinch closed, and secure. Turn right side out.

data.title: Shell-stitch edging
data.source: seed sample, written for this repo
data.text:
Rnd 1: with a 3.0 mm hook and fingering weight cotton, sc evenly around the edge of the finished piece, working 3 sc into each corner. Join with sl st to first sc.
Rnd 2: ch 1, sc in first st, skip 2 sts, *5 dc in next st (shell made), skip 2 sts, sc in next st, skip 2 sts* repeat from * to * around, join to first sc.
Rnd 3: sl st into the centre dc of the first shell, ch 3, 4 dc in same st, *sc in the sc between shells, 5 dc in centre dc of next shell* around, join.
Fasten off. Block the edging flat so the shells open up.

data.title: Terse forum-style pattern (messy input)
data.source: seed sample — deliberately informal, to exercise boundary rules
data.text: ok so magic ring, 6sc. r2 inc all around =12. r3 (sc,inc)*6 =18. r4-6 sc around. r7 (sc,dec)*6 =12. r8 dec*6, close up. 4mm hook, any worsted. took me like 20 min. don't count the ch1 at the start of rows, i never do.

data.title: Abbreviation key only
data.source: seed sample, written for this repo
data.text:
Abbreviations used throughout this document:

ch = chain
sl st = slip stitch
sc = single crochet
hdc = half double crochet
dc = double crochet
tr = treble crochet
blo = back loop only
flo = front loop only
inc = increase (2 stitches worked into one stitch)
dec = decrease (two stitches worked together)
sc2tog = single crochet two together
FO = fasten off
WS / RS = wrong side / right side
st(s) = stitch(es)
rep = repeat
